title: There's a Hole in What You See #science #brain
description:
There's a hole in what you see. Where the optic nerve leaves each eye there are no light sensors at all, so each eye has a blind spot. You never notice it because your brain fills the spot with whatever surrounds it. Try it: close your left eye, stare at the cross with your right eye, and move your phone slowly closer: at one distance the dot on the right vanishes.

More ways your brain edits what you see: Why do wheels spin backwards on camera? https://youtu.be/SxjS9sdc_Ek

Sources
- Purves, D. et al., Neuroscience (Sinauer), chapter on the retina and the optic disc
- Ramachandran, V. S. (1992), Blind spots, Scientific American 266(5): 86–91
- Ramachandran, V. S. & Gregory, R. L. (1991), Perceptual filling in of artificially induced scotomas in human vision, Nature 350: 699–702
